reference.source: Safari reference; Handbook of Interventional Radiological Procedure; Interventional Radiology Cases (topic maps only; prose rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Bleed and ascites are the indications
reference.pathophysiology: TIPS joins hepatic vein to portal branch with a covered stent for refractory bleeding or ascites; the gradient must reach 12 or below while encephalopathy, liver failure and cardiac overload temper selection, and recanalisation or BRTO cover the non-TIPS portal cases.
additionalDifferentials: TIPS versus transplant by reserve and trajectory
Encephalopathy from shunt versus liver failure by course
Gastric versus oesophageal varices by shunt anatomy
additionalInvestigations: Doppler for shunt velocity and direction

figures.title: TIPS Procedure Overview
figures.alt: Diagram illustrating the TIPS procedure: a catheter inserted via the jugular vein, through the vena cava, into a hepatic vein, then puncturing into the portal vein to deploy a stent, creating a shunt within the liver.
figures.caption: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) creation for portal hypertension. Illustration: StewardMD original.
